passages.title: The Lantern Walk
passages.text:
Nora had never been outside after dark without a grown-up holding her hand. So when Ms. Patel announced the class lantern walk through Willow Park, Nora's stomach did a flip.

“Each of you will carry the lantern you made,” Ms. Patel said. “We will walk the loop trail together and listen for owls.”

Nora looked at her lantern. The paper was crooked, and one side was smudged with glue. Her friend Theo's lantern looked like a perfect moon.

On the night of the walk, the park was darker than Nora expected. Shadows stretched across the path like long arms. She held her lantern so tightly that the handle bent.

Halfway around the loop, Theo's candle flickered and went out. He stopped. “I can't see where I'm going,” he whispered.

Nora took a deep breath. She stepped beside him and lifted her crooked lantern high. Its soft orange glow spilled over both of their shoes. “Stay next to me,” she said. “There's enough light for two.”

They walked the rest of the loop side by side. When an owl hooted from a tall oak, Nora didn't flinch. She just smiled and listened.

Back at the school, Theo said, “Your lantern is the best one.” Nora looked at the smudged paper and decided he was right.

passages.title: Busy Builders: How Honeybees Make a Hive
passages.text:
A honeybee hive may look like a messy lump from the outside, but inside it is carefully organized. Thousands of bees work together to build and care for it.

Worker bees make wax inside their own bodies. Special glands on their bellies turn honey into small, thin flakes of wax. The bees chew the flakes to make them soft. Then they press the wax into shape.

Bees build the wax into cells with six sides. A six-sided shape is called a hexagon. Hexagons fit together with no gaps, so the bees do not waste any space. The shape is also strong enough to hold heavy honey.

Each cell has a job. Some cells store honey. Others store pollen, which bees eat for protein. In the center of the hive, the queen lays eggs in empty cells. Young bees grow there until they are ready to leave the cell.

Keeping the hive at the right temperature is important. On hot days, worker bees fan their wings to move air through the hive. On cold days, they cluster together and shiver to make heat.

Without teamwork, a hive could not survive. Every bee has a role, and together they turn a few flakes of wax into a busy home.

passages.title: Grandpa's Rooftop Garden
passages.text:
Every Saturday, Marco climbed the narrow stairs to the roof of his apartment building. That was where Grandpa grew tomatoes, peppers, and beans in old paint buckets.

“Why don't you plant flowers?” Marco asked one morning. “Flowers are prettier.”

Grandpa wiped the dirt from his hands. “Flowers are nice,” he said. “But these plants feed the whole building.”

Marco frowned. He didn't believe that a few buckets could feed anyone.

In August, the plants exploded with vegetables. The tomatoes were as red as fire trucks. The beans dangled like green ribbons. Grandpa handed Marco a basket. “Time to deliver,” he said.

They knocked on Mrs. Lopez's door first. She clapped when she saw the peppers. “Now I can make my famous salsa!” Next, they brought beans to Mr. Kim, who had hurt his knee and couldn't go to the store. He thanked them three times.

By the time the basket was empty, Marco's cheeks hurt from smiling.

The next Saturday, Marco climbed to the roof before Grandpa did. He was holding a small packet of seeds. “Can I have my own bucket?” he asked. “I want to plant carrots for Mr. Kim.”

passages.title: Robots Under the Sea
passages.text:
Most of the ocean floor has never been seen by people. The deep sea is dark, freezing, and full of crushing water pressure. Divers cannot safely go that deep. So scientists send robots instead.

One kind of ocean robot is called an ROV, which stands for remotely operated vehicle. An ROV is connected to a ship by a long cable. Scientists on the ship steer it with controls that look like video game joysticks. Cameras on the ROV send live pictures up the cable.

Another kind of robot swims on its own. These robots are called AUVs, or autonomous underwater vehicles. Before an AUV dives, scientists program a path for it to follow. The AUV collects information about water temperature, saltiness, and the shape of the sea floor. When its mission is over, it returns to the surface so scientists can download the data.

Each type of robot has strengths. An ROV can pick up rocks and animals with its robotic arms, but its cable limits how far it can travel. An AUV can cover huge areas, but it cannot be steered once it dives.

Thanks to these machines, scientists have discovered glowing fish, underwater volcanoes, and coral reefs no one knew existed. The more robots explore, the more we learn about our planet's last great mystery.

passages.title: The Spelling Bee
passages.text:
Ruby practiced her spelling words everywhere. She spelled them while brushing her teeth. She spelled them to her cat, Pepper, who yawned. She even spelled them in the bathtub, writing letters on the foggy mirror.

The school spelling bee was on Friday. Ruby wanted to win more than anything, because the winner got to choose the next class read-aloud book.

On Friday, Ruby stood on the stage with eleven other students. Her knees wobbled like jelly. One by one, students missed words and sat down. Soon only Ruby and a quiet boy named Felix were left.

“Ruby, your word is necessary,” said the principal.

Ruby closed her eyes. She pictured the foggy mirror. “N-E-C-E-S-S-A-R-Y,” she said slowly.

“Correct!”

Then Felix got the word rhythm. He paused. “R-H-Y-T-H-M,” he said.

“Correct!”

The two of them spelled for ten more rounds. Finally, Ruby missed the word mischievous. She had added an extra i. Felix spelled it correctly and won.

Ruby felt a lump in her throat. But then Felix walked over. “You were amazing,” he said. “Want to help me pick the book?”

Ruby grinned. Losing didn't feel so bad after all.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the theme of a story from details in the text.
questions.question: Which sentence best states a theme of the story?
choices: It is important to finish a walk quickly.
Helping someone else can give you courage.
Parks are too dangerous to visit at night.
Homemade crafts should always look perfect.
questions.correctAnswer: Helping someone else can give you courage.
questions.explanation: Nora forgets her fear when she helps Theo, and she even smiles at the owl.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Describe how a character changes and support the answer with evidence.
questions.question: This question has two parts. Answer Part A, then answer Part B.

parts.label: Part A
parts.question: Part A: How does Nora change from the beginning of the story to the end?
choices: She goes from feeling confident to feeling scared.
She goes from feeling bored to feeling excited.
She goes from feeling nervous to feeling confident.
She goes from feeling proud to feeling embarrassed.
correctAnswers: She goes from feeling nervous to feeling confident.

parts.label: Part B
parts.question: Part B: Which sentence from the story best supports the answer to Part A?
choices: The paper was crooked, and one side was smudged with glue.
When an owl hooted from a tall oak, Nora didn't flinch.
Her friend Theo's lantern looked like a perfect moon.
“We will walk the loop trail together and listen for owls.”
correctAnswers: When an owl hooted from a tall oak, Nora didn't flinch.

questions.explanation: At first Nora's stomach flips, but by the end she doesn't flinch at the owl.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative language.
questions.question: In paragraph 4, what does the phrase “Shadows stretched across the path like long arms” help the reader understand?
choices: Nora was playing a game with Theo.
The park seemed spooky to Nora.
The trees were being cut down.
questions.correctAnswer: The park seemed spooky to Nora.
questions.explanation: The simile compares shadows to reaching arms, which shows how scary the dark park felt.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Refer to details in the text when explaining what the text says.
questions.question: Select two details that show Nora was nervous on the night of the walk.
choices: She held her lantern so tightly that the handle bent.
Theo's lantern looked like a perfect moon.
Back at the school, Theo said, “Your lantern is the best one.”
Ms. Patel announced the class lantern walk.
The park was darker than Nora expected.
correctAnswers: The park was darker than Nora expected.
She held her lantern so tightly that the handle bent.
questions.explanation: Both details show Nora's worry about the dark.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how a character's actions contribute to the events.
questions.question: Why does Theo say Nora's lantern is “the best one” at the end of the story?
choices: Her lantern was the neatest in the class.
Her lantern was the biggest one in the park.
Her lantern helped both of them finish the walk.
Her lantern was made by Ms. Patel.
questions.correctAnswer: Her lantern helped both of them finish the walk.
questions.explanation: Theo's candle went out, and Nora's lantern lit the way for both of them.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Distinguish point of view.
questions.question: From which point of view is the story told?
choices: third person, focusing on Ms. Patel's thoughts
third person, focusing on Nora's thoughts and feelings
questions.correctAnswer: third person, focusing on Nora's thoughts and feelings
questions.explanation: The narrator uses “she” and tells what Nora feels, such as her stomach doing a flip.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how key details support it.
questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Honeybees work together to build and care for an organized hive.
Hives are messy on the inside and the outside.
Honeybees eat pollen to get protein.
The queen bee is the only bee that works.
questions.correctAnswer: Honeybees work together to build and care for an organized hive.
questions.explanation: The passage explains how bees build wax cells, store food, raise young, and control temperature as a team.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how and why events or steps happen in a scientific text.
questions.question: This question has two parts. Answer Part A, then answer Part B.

parts.label: Part A
parts.question: Part A: Why do honeybees build cells in the shape of a hexagon?
choices: Hexagons fit together without gaps and are strong.
Hexagons are the only shape wax can make.
Hexagons are the easiest shape for the queen to see.
Hexagons keep the hive cool on hot days.
correctAnswers: Hexagons fit together without gaps and are strong.

parts.label: Part B
parts.question: Part B: Which sentence from the passage best supports the answer to Part A?
choices: On hot days, worker bees fan their wings to move air through the hive.
A six-sided shape is called a hexagon.
Hexagons fit together with no gaps, so the bees do not waste any space.
In the center of the hive, the queen lays eggs in empty cells.
correctAnswers: Hexagons fit together with no gaps, so the bees do not waste any space.

questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 explains that hexagons leave no gaps and are strong enough to hold honey.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the meaning of domain-specific words.
questions.question: In paragraph 5, what does the word cluster mean?
questions.explanation: The bees cluster together to make heat, so they gather closely.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use details from the text to answer questions.
questions.question: Select two ways worker bees control the temperature of the hive.
choices: They lay eggs in empty cells.
They shiver together on cold days.
They fan their wings on hot days.
correctAnswers: They fan their wings on hot days.
They shiver together on cold days.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 describes fanning on hot days and shivering in a cluster on cold days.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Describe the overall structure of a text.
questions.question: How is paragraph 2 mainly organized?
choices: It describes the steps bees follow to make and shape wax.
It tells a story about one bee's life.
It explains a problem and offers a solution.
It compares honeybees to other insects.
questions.correctAnswer: It describes the steps bees follow to make and shape wax.
questions.explanation: The paragraph goes in order: make flakes, chew them, press the wax into shape.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support points.
questions.question: Which detail best supports the author's point that “every bee has a role”?
choices: A hive may look like a messy lump from the outside.
Some bees store food, the queen lays eggs, and workers control the temperature.
questions.correctAnswer: Some bees store food, the queen lays eggs, and workers control the temperature.
questions.explanation: This detail lists different jobs that different bees do.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the theme of a story.
questions.question: What is the central message of the story?
choices: Flowers are more useful than vegetables.
Gardening on a roof is very difficult.
Grandparents always know the right answer.
Sharing what you grow can bring joy to others and to yourself.
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing what you grow can bring joy to others and to yourself.
questions.explanation: Delivering vegetables makes the neighbors happy and makes Marco smile.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Describe characters and explain how their actions contribute to events.
questions.question: This question has two parts. Answer Part A, then answer Part B.

parts.label: Part A
parts.question: Part A: How do Marco's feelings about the garden change?
choices: He doubts it is useful at first, but later he wants to help grow food.
He wants to plant flowers at first and still does at the end.
He is afraid of the roof at first, but later he likes the view.
He loves it at first, but later he finds it boring.
correctAnswers: He doubts it is useful at first, but later he wants to help grow food.

parts.label: Part B
parts.question: Part B: Which sentence best shows how Marco feels at the end of the story?
choices: “I want to plant carrots for Mr. Kim.”
That was where Grandpa grew tomatoes, peppers, and beans in old paint buckets.
correctAnswers: “I want to plant carrots for Mr. Kim.”

questions.explanation: At first Marco doesn't believe buckets can feed anyone; at the end he asks for his own bucket to grow carrots.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the meaning of figurative language.
questions.question: What does the author mean by “the plants exploded with vegetables” in paragraph 5?
choices: The plants were thrown off the roof.
The plants were damaged by a storm.
The plants made a loud noise.
The plants grew many vegetables quickly.
questions.correctAnswer: The plants grew many vegetables quickly.
questions.explanation: “Exploded” is an exaggeration showing that a large number of vegetables suddenly grew.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Refer to details in the text.
questions.question: Select two details that support Grandpa's claim that the plants “feed the whole building.”
choices: Mr. Kim, who couldn't go to the store, gets beans.
Marco asks why Grandpa doesn't plant flowers.
Grandpa grows plants in old paint buckets.
Marco climbs the narrow stairs every Saturday.
Mrs. Lopez can make her salsa with the peppers.
correctAnswers: Mrs. Lopez can make her salsa with the peppers.
Mr. Kim, who couldn't go to the store, gets beans.
questions.explanation: These details show neighbors receiving food from the garden.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how parts of a story build on one another.
questions.question: How does the last paragraph connect to the beginning of the story?
choices: Marco now climbs to the roof eagerly, showing how much he has changed.
It introduces a new problem with the garden.
It shows that Grandpa decided to plant flowers.
It explains why the stairs are narrow.
questions.correctAnswer: Marco now climbs to the roof eagerly, showing how much he has changed.
questions.explanation: The story begins with Marco questioning the garden and ends with him arriving first with seeds.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the main idea and summarize the text.
questions.question: Which sentence best summarizes the passage?
choices: Scientists use two kinds of robots to explore deep parts of the ocean that people cannot reach.
AUVs are better than ROVs in every way.
Glowing fish live near underwater volcanoes.
Divers can explore the deepest parts of the ocean with joysticks.
questions.correctAnswer: Scientists use two kinds of robots to explore deep parts of the ocean that people cannot reach.
questions.explanation: The passage explains why robots are needed and describes ROVs and AUVs.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Describe the structure of a text (compare and contrast).
questions.question: This question has two parts. Answer Part A, then answer Part B.

parts.label: Part A
parts.question: Part A: How is paragraph 4 organized?
choices: It explains the meaning of the word autonomous.
It compares the strengths and limits of two types of robots.
It describes a problem divers faced and how they solved it.
It lists events in the order they happened.
correctAnswers: It compares the strengths and limits of two types of robots.

parts.label: Part B
parts.question: Part B: Which sentence from paragraph 4 best supports the answer to Part A?
choices: Before an AUV dives, scientists program a path for it to follow.
Most of the ocean floor has never been seen by people.
Cameras on the ROV send live pictures up the cable.
An AUV can cover huge areas, but it cannot be steered once it dives.
correctAnswers: An AUV can cover huge areas, but it cannot be steered once it dives.

questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 uses words like “but” to compare what each robot can and cannot do.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the meaning of academic and domain-specific words.
questions.question: Based on paragraph 3, what does autonomous most likely mean?
choices: able to glow in the dark
able to act on its own
questions.correctAnswer: able to act on its own
questions.explanation: The paragraph says AUVs swim “on their own,” following a programmed path.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use details from the text to explain what it says.
questions.question: Select two reasons the passage gives for why scientists send robots instead of divers.
choices: The deep sea has crushing water pressure.
Divers do not like cold water.
The deep sea is dark and freezing.
Robots can see better than cameras.
correctAnswers: The deep sea has crushing water pressure.
The deep sea is dark and freezing.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 explains that the deep sea is dark, freezing, and has crushing pressure.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how and why something happens based on the text.
questions.question: What happens after an AUV finishes its mission?
choices: It sends live pictures up a cable.
Scientists steer it back with joysticks.
It stays on the sea floor forever.
It returns to the surface so scientists can download its data.
questions.correctAnswer: It returns to the surface so scientists can download its data.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 says it returns to the surface so scientists can download the data.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how an author supports a point with reasons.
questions.question: Why does the author include the examples of glowing fish, underwater volcanoes, and coral reefs?
choices: to explain how ROVs are steered
to describe what divers see in shallow water
to show what scientists have discovered by using ocean robots
to compare different kinds of fish
questions.correctAnswer: to show what scientists have discovered by using ocean robots
questions.explanation: These are discoveries made “thanks to these machines.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the theme of a story.
questions.question: Which statement best describes a theme of the story?
choices: Being a good sport can make losing easier.
Spelling bees are unfair to quiet students.
questions.correctAnswer: Being a good sport can make losing easier.
questions.explanation: Felix's kindness after the bee helps Ruby feel better about losing.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Make inferences and support them with text evidence.
questions.question: This question has two parts. Answer Part A, then answer Part B.

parts.label: Part A
parts.question: Part A: What can the reader infer about Ruby based on paragraph 1?
choices: She is worried about her cat.
She is determined to do well.
correctAnswers: She is determined to do well.

parts.label: Part B
parts.question: Part B: Which detail best supports the answer to Part A?
choices: She spelled them to her cat, Pepper, who yawned.
She even spelled them in the bathtub, writing letters on the foggy mirror.
The school spelling bee was on Friday.
correctAnswers: She even spelled them in the bathtub, writing letters on the foggy mirror.

questions.explanation: Practicing even in the bathtub shows how determined Ruby is.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Determine the meaning of figurative language.
questions.question: What does the phrase “Her knees wobbled like jelly” show about Ruby?
choices: She was hungry for a snack.
She was dancing on the stage.
questions.explanation: The simile shows Ruby's knees shaking from nerves.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain how a part of a story fits into its overall structure.
questions.question: How does picturing the foggy mirror help Ruby during the spelling bee?
choices: It makes her laugh and relax.
It helps her see the audience better.
It reminds her of how she practiced, so she spells the word correctly.
It makes her forget the word.
questions.correctAnswer: It reminds her of how she practiced, so she spells the word correctly.
questions.explanation: Ruby connects back to her practice from paragraph 1 and spells “necessary” correctly.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Describe characters' traits using details.
questions.question: Select two words that describe Felix based on his actions at the end of the story.
correctAnswers: kind
generous
questions.explanation: Felix compliments Ruby and invites her to help pick the book.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Ensure subject-verb agreement.
questions.question:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

The puppies ___ in the backyard every afternoon.
questions.explanation: “Puppies” is plural, so it needs the plural verb “play.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.
questions.question:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

Yesterday, Mia ___ a thank-you note to her grandmother.
questions.explanation: “Write” is irregular; its simple past tense is “wrote.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives.
questions.question:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

Of all five puppies, the brown one is the ___.
questions.explanation: When comparing more than two things, use the superlative “smallest.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Form and use irregular plural nouns.
questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct plural noun?
choices: Three goose waddled across the road.
Three geese waddled across the road.
Three gooses waddled across the road.
Three geeses waddled across the road.
questions.correctAnswer: Three geese waddled across the road.
questions.explanation: The plural of “goose” is the irregular noun “geese.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use commas in addresses.
questions.question: Which shows the address written correctly?
questions.explanation: Put a comma between the city and the state.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: “Let's go to the library, said Maya.”
“Let's go to the library” said Maya.
“Let's go to the library,” said Maya.
Let's go to the library, “said Maya.”
questions.correctAnswer: “Let's go to the library,” said Maya.
questions.explanation: The comma goes inside the closing quotation mark, and only the spoken words are inside the quotation marks.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Form and use possessives.
questions.question: Which sentence uses the possessive correctly?
choices: The two dogses leashes were tangled.
The two dog's leashes were tangled.
The two dogs' leashes were tangled.
The two dogs leashes' were tangled.
questions.correctAnswer: The two dogs' leashes were tangled.
questions.explanation: For a plural noun ending in s, add an apostrophe after the s: dogs'.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Capitalize appropriate words in titles and names.
questions.question: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
choices: Last july, we visited Liberty State Park in Jersey City.
Last July, we visited Liberty State Park in Jersey City.
Last July, we visited liberty state park in Jersey City.
Last July, We visited Liberty State Park in jersey city.
questions.correctAnswer: Last July, we visited Liberty State Park in Jersey City.
questions.explanation: Months, names of places, and cities are proper nouns.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
questions.question:
Which word best completes the sentence?

I wanted to play outside, ___ it was raining.
questions.explanation: “But” shows contrast between wanting to play and the rain.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Interpret similes and metaphors in context.
questions.question:
What does the simile mean?

After recess, the classroom was as quiet as a library.
choices: The classroom was full of books.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using “like” or “as.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Explain the meaning of common idioms.
questions.question:
What does the idiom mean?

Dad said the new video game cost an arm and a leg.
choices: Dad hurt himself playing the game.
The game was easy to play.
The game was about a robot.
questions.explanation: “Cost an arm and a leg” means something is very expensive.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words.
questions.question: Which word shows the greatest amount of happiness?
questions.explanation: “Overjoyed” describes the strongest feeling of happiness.

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use context clues to determine the meaning of an unknown word.
questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The trail was so steep that we had to stop and rest many times on the way up.

What does the word steep mean?
questions.explanation: Clues in the sentence show that “steep” means “rising sharply.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use context clues to determine the meaning of an unknown word.
questions.question:
Read the sentence.

Maya was reluctant to jump into the cold lake, so she stood on the dock for a long time.

What does the word reluctant mean?
questions.explanation: Clues in the sentence show that “reluctant” means “not wanting to do something.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use context clues to determine the meaning of an unknown word.
questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The kitten was timid and hid under the bed whenever visitors came over.

What does the word timid mean?
questions.explanation: Clues in the sentence show that “timid” means “shy or easily frightened.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use context clues to determine the meaning of an unknown word.
questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The giant pumpkin was enormous; it took four people to lift it onto the truck.

What does the word enormous mean?
questions.explanation: Clues in the sentence show that “enormous” means “very large.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix un- means “not.” What does the word unhappy mean?
questions.explanation: un- means “not,” so unhappy means “not happy.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix re- means “again.” What does the word rebuild mean?
questions.explanation: re- means “again,” so rebuild means “build again.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix pre- means “before.” What does the word preheat mean?
questions.explanation: pre- means “before,” so preheat means “heat before.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix dis- means “not; opposite of.” What does the word disagree mean?
questions.explanation: dis- means “not; opposite of,” so disagree means “not agree.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix mis- means “wrongly.” What does the word misspell mean?
questions.explanation: mis- means “wrongly,” so misspell means “spell wrongly.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix -less means “without.” What does the word fearless mean?

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix -ful means “full of.” What does the word careful mean?
questions.explanation: -ful means “full of,” so careful means “full of care.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix -able means “able to be.” What does the word washable mean?
questions.explanation: -able means “able to be,” so washable means “able to be washed.”

questions.subject: ela
questions.skill: Use common affixes as clues to the meaning of a word.
questions.question: The affix -er means “one who.” What does the word teacher mean?
questions.explanation: -er means “one who,” so teacher means “one who teaches.”
